description: Public agent skills tested in Driftproof Report #001. Third-party SKILL.md content is NOT committed to this repo; it is fetched at run time from the pinned raw URL below into an untracked workdir (see scripts/fetch-skills.js) and its sha256 is verified against content_sha256. This repo commits only this manifest, our authored eval suites (suites/<slug>/evals.json), the emitted receipts, and the report.
scoping: Report #001 tests TEXT-REPRESENTABLE skills only, supplied as their single SKILL.md file. Bundled reference files loaded on demand (progressive disclosure) are out of scope for this report; skills whose value lives entirely in bundled files (e.g. anthropics/internal-comms) were excluded.

skills.name: Code Review and Quality
skills.description: A five-axis code-review framework and severity-labeling discipline for assessing changes before merge.
skills.author: addyosmani
claims: evaluate every change on correctness, readability/simplicity, architecture, security, performance
approve when the change definitely improves overall code health, even if not perfect
size discipline: ~100 lines ideal, ~1000 signals a needed split
label findings Critical / Required / Optional / Nit
propose the concrete refactor, don't just complain
never accept 'I'll clean it up later'

skills.name: Git Workflow and Versioning
skills.description: Trunk-based git discipline, atomic commits, conventional commit types, and semantic-versioning / changelog conventions.
skills.author: addyosmani
claims: short-lived branches; main always deployable; merge in 1-3 days
atomic, focused commits (separate refactor from feature)
commit messages explain intent using conventional types (feat/fix/refactor/test/docs/chore)
SemVer: breaking = major, feature = minor, fix = patch
tag releases immutably
curate changelogs by user impact, not commit archaeology

skills.name: Documentation and ADRs
skills.description: When and how to write Architecture Decision Records, inline comments, and API docs; document the why.
skills.author: addyosmani
claims: document the why, not the what
write ADRs for costly-to-reverse decisions
match existing repo doc conventions before inventing new ones
never delete old ADRs — supersede them
comment intent, not implementation
public APIs require documented params / returns / exceptions / examples

skills.name: Commit Work
skills.description: Producing high-quality git commits: staging discipline, logical splitting, Conventional Commits messages.
skills.author: Softaworks
claims: commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary
split by logical boundary (feature vs refactor, tests vs prod, deps vs behavior)
use git add -p for mixed files
inspect git status / diff / diff --stat before staging
verify with git diff --cached before committing
a commit should be describable in two sentences

skills.name: Writing Clearly and Concisely
skills.description: Strunk-style prose rules for docs, commit / error messages, reports, and UI text.
skills.author: Softaworks
claims: prefer the active voice
put statements in positive form
use concrete, specific language
omit needless words
keep related words together
place the emphatic word at the end of the sentence

skills.name: Crafting Effective READMEs
skills.description: Audience-first README structure with mandatory sections and project-type templates.
skills.author: Softaworks
claims: design for the specific audience
three mandatory sections: Name, Description (what + why in 1-2 sentences), Usage with examples
structure varies by project type (OSS / personal / internal / config)
lead with the one-sentence problem the project solves
validate the draft against the actual project files
categorize the task (Creating / Adding / Updating / Reviewing) first

skills.name: Naming Analyzer
skills.description: Variable / function / class naming conventions and how to suggest clearer names.
skills.author: Softaworks
claims: language-specific casing (camelCase / PascalCase / snake_case / UPPER_SNAKE_CASE)
boolean names take is / has / can / should prefixes
avoid vague names (data / info / temp / single letters)
names must reflect mutation / behavior
constants include units (e.g. ONE_HOUR_IN_MS)
minimize abbreviations except well-known ones (HTML / API / URL)

skills.name: Requesting Code Review
skills.description: How to prepare and package a change for review: context, base/head SHAs, and severity triage of feedback.
skills.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
claims: supply crafted context to the reviewer, never raw session history
collect BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA for the change
fill the reviewer template with description / requirements / SHAs
triage findings Critical / Important / Minor
mandatory review triggers (after a task, after a major feature, before merge to main)
never self-review inline diffs or skip 'simple' changes

skills.name: Writing Plans
skills.description: How to author a concrete, self-contained implementation plan before coding.
skills.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
claims: concrete over abstract — no TBD / placeholder steps
self-contained tasks, each carrying its own test cycle
exact signatures / types / names, consistent across tasks
bite-sized 2-5 minute steps
files that change together live together (split by responsibility, not layer)
verify each spec requirement maps to a task before handoff

skills.name: Skill Creator
skills.description: Conventions for authoring a SKILL.md: description-as-trigger, progressive disclosure, instructional tone.
skills.author: Anthropic, PBC
skills.license_note: Per-folder LICENSE.txt (Apache-2.0); the anthropics/skills repo has no single top-level LICENSE.
claims: the description is the triggering mechanism — make it specific and list applicable contexts
three-layer progressive disclosure (metadata ~100 words / body < 500 lines / bundled resources on demand)
define the output format with exact templates
prefer theory-of-mind 'why' instructions over rigid all-caps MUSTs
organize domain variants into reference files with pointers from SKILL.md

report_006_pins.note: Report #006 (revision drift, spec 009) current-text arm. Third-party skill content is NOT committed; these are the upstream HEAD pins as of the 2026-08-28 scan, fetched and sha256-verified by scripts/fetch-skills.js exactly as the report-001 pins are. Only skills the scan showed revised appear here; the other seven are byte-identical to their report-001 pins and need no second entry.

suite_pins.note: OUR OWN suite pins, alongside the upstream skill pins above. suite_hash is the runner semantic hash (sha256Canonical over {id,prompt,rubric,pass_threshold}) — the same units receipts record in suite.suite_hash, so a receipt binds to a rubric. evals_sha256 is the committed evals.json bytes, which catches every field suite_hash deliberately excludes (grounding, metadata). Both are asserted by the repo gate: a rubric edit without a re-pin fails.
suite_pins.comparable_note: Reports whose pages claim the same suites. report-007-rerun is a receipts directory rather than a report: Report 007 publishes one cell from a clean re-run held there, and it is declared so that receipt falls under the same pinned-suite assertion as the rest. The gate requires every slug shared by these reports to carry one suite_hash, equal to the pin. A future rubric change means the new report is NOT added here until its page states what changed.
